findings.element: Section 2 condition row — the On the invoice select when Comparison is is empty or is not empty
findings.finding: Choosing is empty disables the invoice-side select that the engine actually evaluates while leaving the payment-side select live and editable, so the row reads as a claim about the payment but is executed against the invoice.
findings.user_impact: The user builds a condition that tests the opposite field from the one the row appears to name, and cannot pick which invoice field is tested unless they set the operand last — choosing it first locks the target to whatever value happened to be there.
findings.suggested_fix: For the two value-less operands, disable and visually mute the On the payment select instead of On the invoice, keep the invoice target editable, and render the row label as the invoice's <target> is empty.

evidence.action: Set a condition row Comparison to is empty and compared the row controls against the engine evaluation and the In plain terms sentence.
evidence.observed: The On the invoice select renders disabled while On the payment stays editable; the engine tests only the invoice doc/memo value and ignores the payment source entirely, and In plain terms correctly prints the invoice's memo on statement is empty — contradicting the row above it.

findings.element: Section 1 scope — the toggle on the date row when the organization is not admin-enabled for no-limit
findings.finding: The toggle is styled identically to the live toggles beside it and silently does nothing on click — no state change, no message, no dimming — while the other gated toggle in the same overlay is visibly dimmed.
findings.user_impact: A user who wants no date limit clicks a control that looks fully interactive and gets zero response, the exact dead-click pattern that KF-4 flags.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the gated date toggle the same dimmed treatment already used for the plan-gated master toggle.

evidence.action: With the admin no-limit flag off, clicked the date row toggle twice.
evidence.observed: State stayed on with no visible reaction; the wrapper only sets cursor:not-allowed and the toggle keeps the standard active styling, whereas the plan-gated master toggle uses the dimmed treatment at opacity .5.

findings.element: Section 3 outcomes — No matching open invoice was found row, and the same phrase in the master-switch copy and the GSP row
findings.finding: The off branch of the no-match outcome is described only as the payment is processed as usual and is never expanded into what Synder actually creates, while the on branch is concrete (nothing is created).
findings.user_impact: Half of the user stated goal — understanding what happens when no invoice is found — is left unanswered for the branch that is the default.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace processed as usual in this row with the concrete artifact Synder creates when the sync is not cancelled.

evidence.action: Read the no-match outcome copy in section 3, in the master-switch description and on the GSP row, then ran the simple-charge sample payment.
evidence.observed: All four places say processed as usual — the nearest expansion is as if no open invoice existed — and the simulator no-match outcome likewise names no resulting record.

findings.element: Overlay footer — disabled Save plus the message N things to fix before this can be saved
findings.finding: When Save is blocked, the fixed footer reports only a count while the offending row and its inline error sit in a separately scrolling body that may be far off screen, and the disabled button swallows the click that would ask for more.
findings.user_impact: A user at the bottom of a long overlay is told something is wrong but not what or where, and has to scroll the whole rule hunting for red text before they can save.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the first blocking error in the footer message and make it a link that scrolls its row into view.

evidence.action: Cleared the metadata key to raise a blocking error, then scrolled to the disclosures at the bottom of the overlay and clicked Save.
evidence.observed: Save is disabled and unresponsive; the footer shows only 1 thing to fix before this can be saved. with no field name and no way to reach the section 1 row holding the inline error.

findings.element: GSP settings — Payment application row on the Starter plan: disabled Configure button plus the Pro plan and above chip
findings.finding: The plan gate states the requirement but offers no action, so the row is a dead end for every Starter user who came here to do this task.
findings.user_impact: The user learns the feature exists and that they cannot have it, with nothing on screen to click next.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the gated row offer the upgrade action directly — an enabled link or button to plans alongside the plan sentence.

evidence.action: Set the plan to Starter and inspected the Payment application row and its only control.
evidence.observed: Configure renders disabled with a grey Pro plan and above chip and the sentence Available on Pro, Pro Max and Premium.; there is no enabled control, link or upgrade affordance anywhere in the row, and the overlay fuller explanation is unreachable.
